performance_tasks.brief: A 20-mark titration or volumetric-analysis task with readings, a correctly formatted table, concordance, calculations, conclusion and evaluation.
A 20-mark redox-titration task with readings, a correctly formatted table, concordance, stoichiometric calculations, conclusion and evaluation.
A 20-mark thermometric or enthalpy task with original data, calculation, conclusion, uncertainty and improvement.
A 20-mark rates or gravimetric task with original data, a graph or linear treatment, calculation, conclusion, uncertainty and improvement.
A 20-mark qualitative-analysis task requiring precise observations, use of excess reagent where relevant, deductions and confirmatory tests using supplied notes.
A 20-mark planning and evaluation task covering apparatus, control variables, error, uncertainty, realistic improvements and an extension.

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 50% in this topic (39 objectives against 78 slots) and cannot reach the None% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
